publications.title: The Role of Microsoft Excel in Supporting Data-Driven Economic Decision-Making Among MSME Actors in The Digital
publications.abstract: This article examines the role of Microsoft Excel in supporting data-driven economic decision-making among micro, small, and medium-sized enterprise (MSME) actors in the digital era. The study uses a qualitative literature review by synthesizing academic publications on spreadsheet-based financial recording, digital adoption, accounting information systems, financial literacy, and managerial decision-making. The review indicates that Excel can help MSMEs organize transaction records, summarize sales and expenses, calculate costs and profit, monitor cash flows, manage inventory, compare business performance, and prepare simple financial projections. Functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, IF, SUMIF, sorting, filtering, charts, and PivotTables can convert routine records into information that is easier to interpret. Such information may support decisions concerning pricing, purchasing, stock replenishment, cost control, promotion, and business expansion. Nevertheless, Excel does not automatically guarantee sound decisions. The usefulness of its outputs depends on the completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of the input data, as well as the user's spreadsheet competence and basic financial literacy. Risks include formula errors, duplicate or missing transactions, uncontrolled file versions, and inadequate data security. The article concludes that Excel is best positioned as an accessible transitional and supporting tool within a broader digital financial-management process, not as a substitute for accounting standards, internal controls, or professional judgment.

publications.title: Machine Learning Meets Blockchain: A Domain-Oriented Review of Integration Mechanisms, Applications and Open Challenges
publications.abstract: Blockchain and machine learning (ML) are combined in systems that must learn from multi-party data and keep a verifiable record of what was used and decided. This scoping-style review of a ranked sample covers seven domains: healthcare, finance, supply chain, energy, smart contracts, transportation and education. We searched Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 15 October 2026, ranked 5,195 candidate records, read 345 abstracts in rank order, coded a core corpus of 192 studies and read 38 in full. Federated learning is the most common method (93 of 192 core studies name it), and detection of fraud, intrusions and vulnerabilities is the most common task among the 38. None of the 38 reports a deployment, 24 report a measured ledger figure and two measure ledger energy. Ten use more than one privacy mechanism, and only two report accuracy with and without it. Attack tests are small, and one study tests a Sybil attacker. Studies differ too much to compare, so we do not rank domains. A ledger shows that a record has not changed, not that it was correct when written. The main gaps are realistic evaluation, shared benchmarks and reporting standards, and tested explanations for decisions made inside contracts.

publications.title: EviRank-ICH Commons Metadata: Sources, Automatic Evidence Labels, Queries and Evaluation Partitions
publications.abstract: Metadata accompanying EviRank-ICH, an evidence-aware video retrieval study. The release contains 4,437 collection-specific segment records from 637 distinct Wikimedia Commons source pages, including source provenance and rights information, automatic evidence labels, compiled queries, grouping and fold assignments, same-item task membership, and source-disjoint refit masks. Version 1.1.1 retains all CSV content from Supplemental Data S1 version 1.1 and updates release documentation. All released evidence labels are automatic; raw human-review data are not included. Study-created contributions are licensed under CC BY 4.0; third-party rights remain unchanged. The package contains no code, model weights, embeddings, videos, images, restricted documentary records, or raw human-review returns. QVHighlights and COIN are not redistributed. The associated manuscript is under resubmission; this release is a dataset, not a publication of the manuscript.

publications.title: Super Intelligence Optimization (SIO v1.0): Algorithmic Discovery Protocols for Autonomous B2B SaaS Web Agents
publications.abstract: Modern B2B SaaS procurement has shifted from traditional human-led search to autonomous agent discovery. Buyers increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, and Claude to execute vendor research, synthesize feature comparisons, and calculate ROI. Super Intelligence Optimization (SIO) is an evidence-led operating framework engineered to connect traditional search architecture with the token-constrained ingestion protocols of answering engines. This paper defines the baseline SIO architecture required to transition enterprise web platforms from human-only indexing to autonomous agent discovery, maximizing Share of Model (SoM). Canonical Entity & Architecture: https://rakesh.work/

publications.title: Hypertension treatment geography in Korea, 2011-2024: code and district-year data
publications.abstract: Code and district-year data for the manuscript "Persistent north-south geography of age-standardized hypertension care and within-district changes in public sports facility density across 229 Korean districts, 2011-2024" (submitted to Hypertension Research). Includes the analytic panel (3,206 district-years), age-standardized expected counts, adjacency graph, all result tables, analysis scripts (R-INLA, Python), and the scripts that generate every number, table, and figure in the manuscript and Supplementary Information. All inputs are public aggregated statistics. Files are restricted during peer review and will be made public on acceptance. The archive is split into parts; see HOW_TO_OPEN.txt.

publications.title: Landmark Studio
publications.abstract: Landmark Studio is a single-file browser application for digitizing 2D landmarks and semilandmarks on photographs for geometric morphometrics. It needs no installation, server or internet connection. Features include landmarks, semilandmark curves anchored between landmarks (with optional smoothing), scale setting (ruler, copy between specimens or CSV import), outlines and wireframe lines, data-quality review, and import/export of TPS files compatible with tpsDig2, geomorph and MorphoJ. Interface in English, Spanish and Chinese.

publications.title: Kyrgyz Automatic Punctuation Restoration Benchmark: reproduction archive
publications.abstract: Frozen text pools, canonical split manifest, archived word-level predictions, training configurations, reports and code snapshot for "Automatic Punctuation Restoration for Kyrgyz: A Two-Source Benchmark and Evaluation Study" (ACM TALLIP, under review). Two written sources (Kyrgyz Wikipedia and a Kyrgyz news corpus), S/C/P word labels with Q/E kept in an extended audit, document-level splits after near-duplicate grouping. See README.md for file hashes, use and per-component licenses.

publications.title: Production source files for "English Literature: A Simplified Survey — Whiteboard Video Lessons" (access restricted)
publications.abstract: Production source files for the video series "English Literature: A Simplified Survey — Whiteboard Video Lessons". The package contains the scene scripts of the twelve lessons (Python), the pipeline used to generate narration, render the animated scenes, and assemble the final videos (cover, watermark, credits), and the brand assets. It documents the authorship and creation date of the series. Access to the files is restricted; they are available from the author on request for teaching or research collaboration. Companion record: the published videos and transcripts (see related identifier).

publications.title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
publications.abstract: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.

publications.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
publications.abstract: Efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices requires balancing performance with compute and memory constraints. Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off, while requiring much less computation than in-training counterparts. We propose DictLLM, a dictionary-based compression scheme in which weight matrices within grouped layers are decomposed into a shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, directly obtained from a pre-trained model without further training. Specifically, we cast DictLLM as a four-step post-training optimization. First, we obtain shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices, amortizing rank across grouped layers; second, we sparsify the layer-specific coefficients to the target compression ratio using a dictionary-aware Hessian; and third, we refine the dictionaries given the resulting sparse coefficients. Finally, we aggressively quantize both components using factor-specific Hessian information: input covariance for the dictionaries and the dictionary-aware Hessian for the coefficients. The resulting representation reduces memory footprint by storing a single shared dictionary per layer group, along with sparse layer-specific coefficients. On language modeling and zero-shot reasoning benchmarks, DictLLM consistently outperforms existing post-training low-rank compression methods and pushes the Pareto frontier between model size and performance. DictLLM compresses the original LLaMA-7B model by 5.1x with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity, achieving a 3.6x higher compression ratio than the state-of-the-art low-rank method.
